title: Protestant schools adopt only the forensic sense in justification disputes
source_text: XXI. Porro ex variis vocis justificandi in Scriptura receptis sensibus, Schola Protestantium, in suis de hominis justificatione Disputationibus, primum illum solum adoptarunt, juxta quem justificatio sumitur forensi significatione. Nam per justificationem hominis coram Deo nihil aliud intelligunt quam peccatoris absolutionem, qua liber pronunciatur a poenis peccato debitis, quae sunt a regno coelesti exclusio, & damnatio ad cruciatus aeternos. Adeoque ex eorum mente, justificatio reapse nihil aliud dicit quam poenae condonationem.
pass_a_gloss: Further, from the various senses of the word justifying received in Scripture, the School of the Protestants, in their Disputations on the justification of man, have adopted only that first one, according to which justification is taken in a forensic signification. For by the justification of a man before God they understand nothing else than the absolution of the sinner, by which he is pronounced free from the penalties due to sin, which are exclusion from the heavenly kingdom and damnation to eternal torments. And so in their mind justification in very deed says nothing else than the condonation of penalty.
pass_b_english: Protestant school disputes adopt only the forensic sense of justification.
Before God it means absolving the sinner from due penalties—condonation of punishment.
